title: Hall and Yard
text:
Paragraph 10 is changed from 10 km/h to 8 km/h inside the building. New full section text:
1. The Harborwick site consists of a single-storey warehouse hall of 6,000 m² with 10 m clear internal height, plus a small office annex attached to the hall. The hall contains all operational zones A–F. No storage or operational activity takes place outside the hall except for vehicle movement and dock operations.
2. The site is enclosed by perimeter fencing. The fenced yard area is 3,500 m² and provides circulation for goods vehicles, access to all dock doors, and the marked driver waiting area. Drivers do not enter the hall.
3. The hall is served by eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height, all located on the yard side of the building. Each dock door is equipped with its own dock leveller. The doors are dedicated by direction of flow.
4. Doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are inbound only. Doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 are outbound only. No inbound unloading is permitted at an outbound door and no outbound loading is permitted at an inbound door. Door allocation and time slots are assigned by the dispatcher.
5. Internal circulation is based on a defined aisle network. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and provide the primary routes for materials handling equipment between zones and to and from the docks.
6. Rack storage aisles in the bulk storage area are 3.0 m wide. These aisles are for pallet put-away and retrieval only and are not used as through-routes for general transport unless required for the task.
7. Pedestrian walkways are physically separated from vehicle routes by fixed yellow barriers. All separated walkways are 1.2 m wide and are the only permitted pedestrian routes through operational areas.
8. Where pedestrian and vehicle routes meet, the meeting points are marked as pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramp areas. These areas are clearly signed and marked on the floor.
9. Speed limits apply to all powered equipment, including counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and electric pallet jacks, and to all visiting vehicles in the yard. The limits are enforced in all shifts without exception.
10. Inside the building the maximum speed is 8 km/h. In the yard the maximum speed is 15 km/h. In all marked pedestrian zones, at all pedestrian crossings and on all dock ramps the maximum speed is 5 km/h.
11. The yard layout provides sufficient turning and queuing space for curtain-side trailers and delivery vans to access their assigned doors without obstructing other doors. Vehicles waiting for a slot wait only in the marked waiting area in the yard.
12. Any change to hall layout, yard markings, barriers, dock designation or speed limits requires approval by the warehouse manager before implementation. Temporary obstructions to aisles, walkways or dock approaches are not permitted unless controlled by the shift supervisor.

title: Floor Zones A–F
text:
1. The hall floor is divided into six permanently marked zones, Zone A to Zone F. The zones cover the entire 6,000 m² hall: Zone A 800 m², Zone B 2,200 m², Zone C 1,200 m², Zone D 900 m², Zone E 300 m² and Zone F 600 m². Boundaries are painted on the floor, signed overhead and shown on the site plan at each entrance. All tasks, scanner instructions and shift briefings use zone letters.

2. Zone A is receiving. It lies immediately inside inbound doors 1 to 4 and contains the unloading lanes, inspection benches and document-check area. All inbound goods are received, counted and inspected in Zone A. No pallet moves beyond Zone A until paperwork has been checked and the delivery accepted.

3. Zone B is bulk storage. It occupies 2,200 m² and provides 2,400 pallet positions in high-bay pallet racking. Each rack bay in Zone B is limited to 2,700 kg. Where block stacking is used outside racking, stacks in Zone B are limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high.

4. Zone C is picking. It occupies 1,200 m² and contains ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Zone C holds no bulk reserve stock; all pick faces in Zone C are fed by replenishment from Zone B before each picking shift.

5. Zone D is dispatch. It occupies 900 m² directly in front of outbound doors 5 to 8 and is used solely for outbound staging. Only wrapped, labelled and system-released pallets are placed in Zone D, staged by outbound door and load.

6. Zone E is the cold zone. It is a physically segregated chilled area of 300 m² held between +2 °C and +6 °C. Zone E is fitted with continuous temperature monitoring and audible alarms, supplemented by manual temperature verification in Zone E each shift.

7. Zone F is services and control. It occupies 600 m² and contains value-added packing, the quarantine area and the returns inspection area. Goods in quarantine in Zone F remain physically separated and clearly identified until formally released or written off.

8. Inside Zone F is the separate ventilated hazmat cage. The cage occupies 60 m² within Zone F. All hazardous materials on site are stored only inside this cage in Zone F and never in any other zone. Total quantity in the hazmat cage in Zone F never exceeds 4,000 kg at a time.

9. Movement between zones follows the fixed flow: inbound goods enter Zone A, then booked goods are put away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F; replenishment moves pallets from Zone B to Zone C; picked and packed pallets move from Zone C to Zone D for dispatch. Returns and damaged goods move to Zone F.

10. Storage outside marked zones is not permitted. Pallets, cages, packing materials and waste handling equipment are stored only within their allocated zone. Aisles, pedestrian walkways and dock approaches in all zones are kept clear at all times.

11. Zone designations are fixed. Any change to zone boundaries, zone use or the location of the hazmat cage within Zone F requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and an update to the posted site plan and WMS locations before use.

title: Docks and Yard Access
text:
Paragraph 11 changed: Inside the building the maximum is 8 km/h. Full section:
1. Access to the yard is through the fenced perimeter gates. The yard of 3,500 m² provides one-way circulation for goods vehicles to and from the eight dock doors. Only authorised vehicles, employees and escorted visitors are permitted inside the fence.
2. All eight dock doors are located on the yard side of the hall at 1.2 m dock height. Each door is equipped with its own dock leveller. A leveller is operated only by trained warehouse staff and only for the vehicle currently assigned to that door.
3. Doors are dedicated by flow. Doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are inbound only for unloading. Doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 are outbound only for loading. No door is used for the opposite flow for any reason.
4. Every carrier is assigned a door and a time slot by the dispatcher before arrival. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling. No vehicle approaches a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.
5. On arrival, drivers report to the gate or to the dispatcher and then move only to their assigned door at the assigned time. Drivers remain with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the yard. Drivers never enter the hall.
6. The marked waiting area is the only permitted waiting place for drivers and for vehicles queuing for a slot. Vehicles waiting for a slot wait only there and do not obstruct other dock approaches, yard lanes or pedestrian routes.
7. No unloading or loading begins until the vehicle is correctly positioned at the assigned door, the engine is stopped, the parking brake is applied and the dock leveller is safely deployed by warehouse staff. Dock doors remain closed when not in active use.
8. Inbound operators and forklift operators work inside the hall and on the dock levellers in Zone A at doors 1 to 4 to unload. Dispatch and warehouse staff work in Zone D at doors 5 to 8 to load. Drivers do not operate materials handling equipment, dock levellers or doors.
9. Pedestrian access to the dock area is only via the physically separated 1.2 m wide walkways with fixed yellow barriers. Where walkways meet vehicle lanes, the crossings are marked and signed. No pedestrian walks behind a vehicle at a dock or crosses a dock ramp unless authorised by the shift supervisor.
10. Yard traffic uses the marked lanes to reach the assigned door and to exit without reversing across other doors where possible. Sufficient turning and queuing space is maintained so that a vehicle at one door does not block access to any other door.
11. Speed limits are enforced for all powered equipment and all visiting vehicles. The maximum speed in the yard is 15 km/h. Inside the building the maximum is 8 km/h. At all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps, in the yard and in the hall, the maximum is 5 km/h.
12. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m width provide the link between the docks and Zones A to F. Rack storage aisles of 3.0 m are not used as through-routes to the docks except for put-away and retrieval tasks.
13. Any obstruction to a dock approach, yard lane, walkway or crossing is not permitted. Waste, pallets, stretch wrap materials and handling equipment are not staged in the yard or across dock approaches. The shift supervisor controls any temporary closure of a door or yard lane and informs the dispatcher immediately.
14. Changes to door designations, time-slot arrangements, waiting area location, yard markings, barriers or leveller operating arrangements require prior approval by the warehouse manager before implementation.

title: Roles on Site
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. employs 38 to 40 people on site in defined roles. Every person is assigned to one role with fixed duties by zone and procedure. No task is carried out outside its assigned role and zone.

2. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site, including operations, safety and final sign-offs. The manager is the only person who authorises new forklift operators and overtime and signs off stocktake results and write-offs above 750 EUR.

3. Two shift supervisors provide cover for the two-shift pattern, one supervisor in charge of the floor on each shift. A shift supervisor runs the floor staff, controls the shift workflow between Zones A to F, and leads incident response on that shift.

4. Eight forklift operators operate materials handling equipment. They drive the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for high-bay work in Zone B, and electric pallet jacks for general pallet moves. They work to WMS tasks for put-away, replenishment and loading.

5. Six inbound operators work in Zone A at inbound doors 1 to 4. They check delivery paperwork before unloading, unload vehicles, count and inspect goods, and present accepted goods for system booking. No goods move beyond Zone A until they have completed these checks.

6. Ten pickers work in Zone C. They pick customer orders against scanner-directed tasks from ground-level pick faces and flow racks, scan-verify each pick, and move picked goods for packing and transfer to Zone D.

7. Two stock controllers own inventory accuracy day to day. They plan and execute cycle counts on the rotating zone schedule, carry out second counts and recounts, investigate discrepancies, and prepare adjustments for approval. They do not post adjustments without a second count.

8. Four returns and packing staff work in Zone F. They inspect all returned goods, record condition, and propose disposition as restock, rework or scrap. They also carry out value-added packing tasks in Zone F as directed.

9. One maintenance technician maintains all materials handling equipment, racking and dock equipment including dock levellers. The technician carries out planned checks, repairs and racking inspections and logs every repair and inspection in the maintenance record.

10. Two dispatchers control outbound flow and transport. They book carriers, assign each carrier a door and time slot, manage the yard waiting area, and release outbound loads from Zone D at doors 5 to 8. No vehicle is loaded without dispatcher release.

11. Two floaters provide cover for absence across inbound, picking, packing and dispatch. When covering a role, a floater works only within the duties of that role and under the shift supervisor's direction.

12. Forklift and reach truck operation is restricted to authorised forklift operators only. Authorisation is granted personally by the warehouse manager after licence and training verification. No other role operates those trucks for any reason.

13. All roles operate within procedures PR-01 to PR-15. Shift supervisors direct task allocation on the floor, but role boundaries remain: inbound operators do not pick, pickers do not put away to high bays, and stock controllers do not handle returns disposition except through the count process.

14. Every person on the warehouse floor wears high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear as required for their zone. Each role is responsible for keeping its work area, aisles and dock approaches clear and for reporting hazards to the shift supervisor immediately.

title: Approvals and Accountability
text:
1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site and retains final sign-off for stocktake results and for any damaged-goods write-off above 750 EUR.

2. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 750 EUR, the final disposition of inspected returns, and reviews every incident report on that shift.

3. Damaged-goods write-off thresholds are not aggregatable or splittable to avoid escalation and approvals are not delegable. Each write-off is approved personally by the authorised role and recorded with approver name, date, time, SKU, quantity, value and reference.

4. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count.

5. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling.

6. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime.

7. Stock controllers prepare adjustments; returns staff propose restock, rework or scrap; the maintenance technician logs every repair.

8. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month and an evacuation drill is run every quarter with roll call at the assembly point by the north fence before re-entry.

9. Quarantine and hazmat controls in Zone F remain physically separated, with total quantity in the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage never exceeding 4,000 kg.

10. All operations run under procedures PR-01 to PR-15 in Zones A to F within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager.

11. Responsibilities as defined in this section are fixed and apply to all clients and shifts without exception.

12. Changes to fixed site standards require prior approval by the warehouse manager. This includes any change to hall or yard layout, zone boundaries or zone use, the location of the 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F, the 4,000 kg hazmat limit, aisle widths of 4.0 m and 3.0 m, pedestrian walkway provision of 1.2 m, barriers, dock designations, time-slot arrangements and speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

title: Shift Leadership and Dock Control
text: Paragraph 5 changed to 8 km/h inside. Paragraph 5 now: The shift supervisor enforces standards on the floor, including high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear for everyone on the floor, seat-belt use on forklifts, speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, and the use of physically separated 1.2 m walkways. All other paragraphs unchanged.

title: Working Hours
text:
1. The site operates on a two-shift pattern, Monday to Friday. The morning shift runs 06:00 to 14:00. The afternoon shift runs 14:00 to 22:00. All warehouse activity in Zones A to F and all dock activity at doors 1 to 8 takes place within these hours.

2. No shift operates without its shift supervisor present and in charge of the floor. One shift supervisor is assigned to each shift and remains on site and contactable for the full 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00 period, including during breaks.

3. Standard working hours apply to all roles on site: warehouse manager, shift supervisors, forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, maintenance technician, dispatchers and floaters. Start and finish times are as rostered within the two-shift pattern.

4. The morning and afternoon shifts provide continuous cover Monday to Friday. Handover between shifts takes place at 14:00, with the outgoing supervisor briefing the incoming supervisor on dock status, work in progress and any incidents before leaving the floor, in accordance with PR-15.

5. There is no routine weekend working. Saturday and Sunday are non-working days, except for Saturday morning overtime in peak season as described below. No picking, put-away, receiving or dispatch is scheduled outside Monday to Friday without an approved overtime arrangement.

6. In peak season the site may add Saturday morning overtime to meet outbound and inbound demand. Saturday overtime is limited to the morning period only. No Saturday afternoon, Saturday night or Sunday working is scheduled.

7. Overtime is approved only by the warehouse manager. No other role authorises overtime, extends a shift beyond 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00, or calls staff in for Saturday morning work. Approval is personal and given in advance where possible.

8. Every overtime approval is recorded, including date, shift or Saturday period, roles required and reason. The shift supervisor records the approval and the staff rostered, and ensures only approved staff attend for the approved period.

9. Where overtime is approved, task allocation and safe staffing levels remain under the shift supervisor's control. The supervisor confirms sufficient cover for the planned work across Zones A to F, for dock operations at the assigned doors, and for supervision, first-aid and emergency response.

10. Staff are not permitted to remain on the warehouse floor or in the yard outside their rostered shift or approved overtime period unless directed by the shift supervisor for a specific operational or safety reason. Drivers and visitors are not permitted outside assigned door times for any reason.

11. Any change to the standard pattern of 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 Monday to Friday, or to the arrangements for Saturday morning overtime, requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before publication to staff or to carriers. Temporary obstructions or early closures are controlled by the shift supervisor and notified to the dispatcher immediately.

12. Attendance, absence and lateness during working hours are managed by the shift supervisor on each shift. The supervisor deploys the two floaters to cover absence within the approved shift pattern. If cover cannot be maintained safely, the supervisor escalates to the warehouse manager before reducing dock activity or outbound releases.

title: End-of-Shift Handover
text:
Paragraph 7 updated for cold zone to +2 °C to +6 °C. Full updated paragraph 7 text:

7. Safety and incident status is handed over. The outgoing supervisor reports all injuries, near misses, racking or equipment damage, temperature alarms in Zone E between +2 °C and +6 °C, and spills or quantity changes in the 60 m² hazmat cage in Zone F, with reference to incident reports reviewed on that shift under PR-09, PR-13 and PR-14.

All other paragraphs 1-6 and 8-12 unchanged.

title: Arrival and Door Assignment
text:
ops.ch04.s1 Arrival and Door Assignment

1. All inbound deliveries arrive only at doors 1, 2, 3 and 4. No inbound vehicle is received at doors 5 to 8 for any reason. Inbound receiving in Zone A operates only within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager.

2. Every inbound carrier is assigned a specific door and time slot by the dispatcher before arrival. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling for doors 1 to 4. No assignment is made or changed on the floor without dispatcher confirmation.

3. Carriers are instructed to report arrival to the gate or to the dispatcher and then wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the yard. Drivers never enter the hall and never approach a door until called forward at the assigned time.

4. Vehicles arriving early or late for their slot wait only in the marked waiting area and do not obstruct other dock approaches, yard lanes or pedestrian routes. The dispatcher reschedules late or unscheduled arrivals to the next available inbound slot and informs the shift supervisor.

5. No vehicle moves to a door until the dispatcher has confirmed the door is free and the shift supervisor has confirmed Zone A has capacity to receive. The yard speed limit of 15 km/h and the 5 km/h limit at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps apply to all movements to the door.

6. On being called forward, the driver positions the vehicle squarely at the assigned door, stops the engine, applies the parking brake and hands over delivery documents from the cab or waiting area. The dock door remains closed until staff are ready.

7. Unloading does not begin until the vehicle is correctly positioned and secured and the dock leveller for that door has been safely deployed by trained warehouse staff. Levellers are operated only for the vehicle currently assigned to that door.

8. Under PR-01, document check takes place in Zone A before anything is unloaded. Six inbound operators work in Zone A and check paperwork at the document-check area inside doors 1 to 4. No pallet is removed from the vehicle until the check is complete.

9. The check verifies carrier identity, booking reference, door and time-slot assignment, purchase order or inbound reference, supplier, number of pallets and product description against the expected inbound record. Any seal number is recorded where applicable.

10. If documents are missing, do not match the booking, or refer to unscheduled goods, unloading is held. The inbound operator immediately escalates to the shift supervisor and the dispatcher. No goods move past Zone A and no booking is made in the system until the discrepancy is resolved.

11. Where the document check identifies overage that would breach site limits, including the hazmat cage limit of 4,000 kg in Zone F or the pallet weight limit of 900 kg, the delivery is held in the vehicle or in Zone A in its holding location and the shift supervisor decides acceptance, partial acceptance or refusal with dispatcher support.

12. Accepted deliveries are confirmed as accepted on the paperwork with date, time, door number, name of the checker and signature. Only after this confirmation do inbound operators begin unloading in accordance with PR-01. The dispatcher and shift supervisor update the door board to show the door as occupied for unloading.

13. Drivers remain with their vehicle or in the marked waiting area during unloading, do not operate materials handling equipment, dock levellers or doors, and do not enter Zone A. Any temporary closure of an inbound door or waiting area is controlled by the shift supervisor and notified to the dispatcher immediately.

title: Scan Verification
text:
1. Every item picked in Zone C is scan-verified in the WMS under PR-04 before it is packed under PR-05. No picked item is packed, labelled or moved to Zone D without a successful scan verification on a handheld scanner.

2. Verification is carried out at the pick face by the picker using one of the 20 handheld WMS scanners. The picker scans the pick-face location label and then scans each SKU, batch or case picked, in the quantity directed by the WMS task. The system verifies SKU, batch, expiry where applicable, and quantity against the customer order.

3. Verification is face by face in the sequence directed by the WMS. The picker does not proceed to the next face until the current face is accepted by the system. The scanner displays accepted, short or rejected for each scan.

4. A successful verification requires three matches: location matches task, SKU and batch match order, and quantity matches directed quantity. Only when all three match does the WMS close the pick line and authorise packing for that line.

5. Any scan failure stops the process at that face. Wrong SKU, wrong batch, wrong expiry, wrong quantity or unreadable barcode is not forced or manually overridden on the scanner. The picker leaves the stock in place, records the exception on the scanner as scan-failed, and reports immediately to the shift supervisor.

6. The shift supervisor decides the next action for a failed scan. This includes checking the face, confirming replenishment from Zone B, requesting a stock controller recount, or re-directing the pick to an alternative face. No adjustment is posted without a second count.

7. Damaged, leaking, wet, open or suspect goods found during verification are not scan-verified and not packed. They are segregated at the face, reported to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The quarantine quantity and reason are recorded in the WMS.

8. Short picks are scan-verified as short. Where the face quantity is insufficient, the picker enters the actual quantity picked on the scanner and confirms short pick. The WMS logs the shortage, retains the order line as incomplete and notifies the shift supervisor for replenishment or order amendment.

9. Once all lines for an order or pallet are scan-verified, the WMS authorises packing and labelling for that pallet. Packing under PR-05 begins only after this authorisation. Goods are placed stable and within the pallet footprint, under the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg including load.

10. Labelling is applied only to scan-verified and packed pallets. The picker or packing staff scan the pallet licence plate and apply the WMS-generated label with customer, order and destination data. Hand-written labels or pre-printed labels that do not match the verified pallet record are not permitted.

11. The verified pallet is then closed in the WMS as ready for Zone D. The closure scan records picker name, scanner ID, date and time, and links the pallet to its order and outbound load. Only closed, scan-verified pallets are eligible for transfer to dispatch staging in Zone D.

12. All scan verifications, failures, short picks, quarantine moves and packing completions are recorded automatically in the WMS. The shift supervisor reviews verification exceptions during the shift and includes open verification faults, scanner defects and unresolved short picks in the PR-15 handover record.

13. Any scanner fault, label misprint or system rejection that prevents verification is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The affected pallet remains in Zone C, clearly separated and not moved to Zone D, until the fault is corrected and successful scan verification is completed on a serviceable scanner.

title: Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity
text:
1. Every outbound pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. This 1,000 kg limit is the basis for all vehicle load calculations, rack bay limits of 2,700 kg and staging rules in Zone D. No pallet above 1,000 kg is wrapped, staged or loaded.

2. The contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch are rated at 24,000 kg payload on 33 floor positions. The rating is determined by weight before floor space. At the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg, a trailer therefore takes at most 24 full-weight pallets. No trailer is loaded beyond 24,000 kg for any reason.

3. The 33 floor positions in a trailer are the physical floor count only. Where pallets weigh less than 1,000 kg, additional pallets may be loaded to use floor space, provided the total payload does not exceed 24,000 kg, the load is stable and within the pallet footprint, and the dispatcher has released the load.

4. The delivery van is rated at 1,200 kg payload on 6 floor positions. At the site pallet limit, the van takes at most one full-weight 1,000 kg pallet. No van is loaded beyond 1,200 kg.

5. Any consignment exceeding 1,200 kg, or requiring more than one full-weight pallet, does not go by van. It is assigned to a curtain-side trailer and loaded only at doors 5 to 8 under PR-06.

6. Outbound loading takes place only at doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 at 1.2 m dock height, each with its own dock leveller operated only by trained warehouse staff. No outbound loading is permitted at inbound doors 1 to 4.

7. The dispatcher owns transport booking and door allocation. The dispatcher assigns every outbound carrier a specific door 5 to 8 and time slot, sequences loads by cut-off, and releases each load from Zone D only when wrapped, labelled and closed in the WMS.

8. Outbound capacity per shift is fixed by doors and turn rate. Each of the 4 outbound doors handles 3 trailer loads per shift within rostered hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager.

9. At 24 full-weight pallets per trailer, 3 loads per door and 4 doors in use, the maximum outbound throughput is 12 trailer loads per shift. This equates to 288 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets per shift. This is the most that can be promised to a client for a single shift.

10. Staging in Zone D is planned against this maximum. Each load is staged by door and by drop sequence in its marked 900 m² lane in Zone D, with 4.0 m main transport aisles, physically separated 1.2 m pedestrian walkways and dock approaches kept clear. No staging takes place outside Zone D.

11. No pallet is loaded without dispatcher release and WMS confirmation. Forklift operators scan each pallet licence plate and the door or load reference at doors 5 to 8. Any weight, label, quantity or destination mismatch stops loading and is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and dispatcher.

12. Overweight, unstable, leaning, leaking or damaged pallets are not loaded to any vehicle. They are segregated in Zone D, reported to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The hazmat cage limit of 4,000 kg in the 60 m² cage in Zone F, meaning at most 4 full-weight pallets, is applied separately and no hazmat is loaded except from that cage under PR-13.

13. Load documents record carrier, door, time slot, trailer or van identity, pallet count, total weight and dispatcher release with date, time and names. No vehicle leaves the yard without completed paperwork and dispatcher confirmation. Any change to vehicle ratings, door allocation, turn rate or the 288-pallet shift maximum requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before use.

title: Aisle Network and Walkways
text:
1. The internal circulation network provides physical separation between people and materials handling equipment at all times. Pedestrians and powered trucks use different, barriered routes. No shared unprotected route is permitted in the hall, in Zone F or at the docks.

2. Pedestrian walkways are physically separated from vehicle routes by fixed yellow barriers. The barriers are continuous, floor-fixed and impact-rated. No pallet, cage, packing material or waste is placed on, against or over a barrier and no gap is left open for convenience.

3. All separated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. The width is measured clear between barriers or between barrier and wall. The walkways are the only permitted pedestrian routes through operational areas in Zones A to F and to and from the office annex.

4. Walkways are permanently marked on the floor with solid white borders and green infill, signed overhead with pedestrian symbols and shown on the site plan at each entrance. Lighting, floor markings and signage are maintained so that the walkway is visible along its full length.

5. Main transport aisles provide the primary routes for counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and electric pallet jacks between Zones A to F and to and from dock doors 1 to 8. Every main transport aisle is 4.0 m wide, measured clear between racking, barriers or walls.

6. Main transport aisles are for through movement of loaded and unladen equipment only. No storage, staging, packing, quarantine or waste handling takes place in a main transport aisle, and the aisle is kept clear for its full 4.0 m width.

7. Rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide. These aisles are for pallet put-away and retrieval in the 2,400-position high-bay racking only. They are not used as through-routes for general transport between zones unless the WMS task requires entry to that aisle.

8. Where pedestrian and vehicle routes meet, the meeting points are designed as marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps. Each crossing is signed, hatched on the floor and controlled by barriers, gates or speed reduction. No crossing is created without fixed signage and markings.

9. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m separated walkways and the marked crossings. Stepping outside a walkway into a main transport aisle of 4.0 m, into a rack aisle of 3.0 m or behind a vehicle at a dock is not permitted. Drivers and operators remain on vehicle routes and do not walk through walkways while driving.

10. Forklifts, reach trucks and electric pallet jacks remain on vehicle routes. Entry to a pedestrian walkway by any powered truck, hand pallet jack or loaded pallet is not permitted for any reason, including short cuts or temporary staging.

11. Physical separation is maintained at zone interfaces. Walkways connect Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone and Zone F services and control without requiring pedestrians to cross unprotected vehicle lanes. Doors to Zone E and gates to the 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F open directly off walkways or controlled crossings.

12. All barriers, floor markings and crossing points are inspected as part of the monthly racking and equipment inspection by the maintenance technician and logged. Any damage to a yellow barrier, missing marking, obscured sign or blocked walkway is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and repaired before the route is returned to use.

13. Any change to the aisle network, walkway provision of 1.2 m, barrier type or position, aisle widths of 4.0 m and 3.0 m, or to the location of pedestrian zones, crossings or dock ramps requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and an update to the posted site plan before use.

title: Speed Limits
text: Paragraph 3 changed: Inside the building the maximum speed is 8 km/h. This applies everywhere inside the hall, including Zones A to F, main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack storage aisles of 3.0 m, packing areas and staging lanes, and to all powered equipment. All other paragraphs unchanged.

title: Pedestrian Safety Rules
text: Paragraph 7 changed: At every marked pedestrian zone, at every pedestrian crossing and on every dock ramp the maximum speed for all powered equipment is 5 km/h, whether pedestrians are present or not. Inside the building the maximum elsewhere is 8 km/h; in the 3,500 m² fenced yard the maximum is 15 km/h. The 5 km/h areas start at the posted signs and floor markings. All other paragraphs unchanged.

title: Electric Fleet
text:
1. The site operates an all-electric materials handling fleet. No internal-combustion, LPG or diesel trucks are used in the hall or in the yard. All charging is from the designated charging area and only by trained staff.

2. The fleet consists of 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks. No other pallet-moving equipment is held on site.

3. The 6 counterbalance forklifts at 2.5 t rated capacity are the general-work trucks. They carry out unloading and loading at the 8 dock doors at 1.2 m dock height, transport between Zones A to F on the 4.0 m main transport aisles, and put-away and retrieval to lower levels in Zone B.

4. The 4 reach trucks at 1.6 t rated capacity are for high-bay work in Zone B only. They serve the 2,400 pallet positions in high-bay racking and operate exclusively in the 3.0 m rack storage aisles and the adjoining transfer lanes.

5. Ratings of 2.5 t and 1.6 t are manufacturer rated capacities at rated load centre. The operational limit on site is lower and governs every lift: every pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. No lift above 1,000 kg per pallet is permitted on any truck, including unladen-rated travel.

6. The 1,000 kg pallet limit is the basis for all storage limits in Zone B. Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg total, and block stacking outside racking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high. The WMS blocks any put-away that would exceed these limits.

7. The 8 electric pallet jacks are powered pedestrian or ride-on jacks for horizontal pallet moves. They are used for Zone A transfer to booking, replenishment support from Zone B to Zone C, and movement of wrapped pallets in Zone D to the staging lanes for doors 5 to 8.

8. The 12 hand pallet jacks are manual, non-powered jacks for small moves. They are used in Zone C for order tote and pallet positioning, in Zone F for packing and returns handling, and for short repositioning where powered equipment is not required. They are pushed at walking pace only.

9. The fleet does not include order-picking trucks, very-narrow-aisle trucks or tow tractors. Pickers do not drive counterbalance forklifts or reach trucks. Only forklift operators authorised personally by the warehouse manager drive the 2.5 t counterbalance and 1.6 t reach trucks.

10. All dock doors 1 to 8 are served by the counterbalance fleet and electric pallet jacks via their own dock levellers. Levellers are operated only by trained warehouse staff for the vehicle currently assigned to that door. No driver operates MHE or levellers.

11. The site also holds 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D and 1 cardboard baler, plus 20 handheld WMS scanners shared across tasks. These are not MHE and do not lift loads. Wrapping, baling and scanning are carried out only by trained staff under PR-05 and PR-10.

12. Rated capacities are displayed on each truck's data plate and are not altered, uprated or derated locally. Any attachment, modification or repair affecting capacity, stability, braking or steering is reported to the shift supervisor and approved by the warehouse manager before return to service, with the maintenance technician logging the work.

13. No truck lifts more than its rated capacity and no pallet exceeds 1,000 kg. Any pallet indicating overweight, instability, collapse or unsafe wrapping is held in its zone and not lifted to height. It is segregated and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

14. Any change to fleet numbers, truck types, rated capacities of 2.5 t and 1.6 t, or to the 1,000 kg pallet limit requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and an update to training, WMS limits and the posted fleet list before use.

title: Authorisation and Daily Checks
text: Paragraph 12 changed: Defects affecting safety, capacity or stability — including brakes, steering, forks, chains, seat belt, battery, leveller interlock at the 1.2 m dock doors, or any damage affecting the 1,000 kg pallet limit or the 2,700 kg rack bay limit in Zone B — are escalated to the warehouse manager for approval before return to service. The repair is logged by the maintenance technician. AND the enforceable limits sentence in paragraph 12 updated: A truck that passes its daily check remains subject to continuous monitoring. Any fault arising during the shift is reported at once to the shift supervisor, the task is stopped and the truck is tagged out under paragraph 10. Speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m² yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps remain enforceable on all serviceable trucks. All other paragraphs unchanged.

title: Safe Operation
text: Paragraph 4 changed: Three speed limits apply to all powered equipment and are enforced on every shift without exception. Inside the building the maximum speed is 8 km/h. In the 3,500 m² fenced yard the maximum speed is 15 km/h. At all marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and on all dock ramps the maximum speed is 5 km/h. Paragraph 5 changed: The 8 km/h building limit applies everywhere inside the hall, including Zones A to F, main transport aisles, rack storage aisles, packing areas in Zone F, staging lanes in Zone D and the cold zone Zone E. The 15 km/h limit applies to all yard circulation lanes, approaches to doors 1 to 8 and the marked driver waiting area. All other paragraphs unchanged.

title: Returns Intake and Inspection
text:
1. Returns handling is carried out under PR-07 in Zone F. All returned goods are received, recorded and inspected only in the returns inspection area in Zone F. No returns are received, inspected or stored in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D or Zone E, and no returns are handled at outbound doors 5 to 8.

2. Harborwick accepts returns within 14 days of the original delivery date only. The delivery date is taken from the outbound manifest and proof of delivery for that load. The 14-day window is counted as calendar days from delivery to presentation at the site.

3. Returned goods arrive at an assigned inbound door 1 to 4 at a time slot agreed with the dispatcher. The driver reports to the gate or dispatcher and waits with the vehicle or in the marked waiting area in the yard. Drivers never enter the hall and never move goods to Zone F.

4. Before unloading, inbound operators and the shift supervisor check the returns paperwork in Zone A: customer name, original order and outbound load reference, delivery date, SKU and quantity presented as return, and reason for return. No pallet is removed until the 14-day eligibility is confirmed.

5. Where the documents show the delivery was more than 14 days ago, where the customer or order cannot be matched, or where the quantity would breach site limits including the 1,000 kg pallet limit, the return is refused at the door. The refusal is recorded with date, time, door, carrier and reason and countersigned by the shift supervisor.

6. Accepted returns are moved directly to the returns inspection area in Zone F. They are booked in the WMS to returns status on arrival, with customer, original order, delivery date, return date, SKU, quantity, pallet identity and reason. They are physically separated, clearly signed as returns and not available for picking, replenishment or dispatch.

7. Every unit presented as a return is individually inspected in Zone F. Inspection is carried out by the 4 returns and packing staff under PR-07. No bulk acceptance, sample check or visual pass from a distance replaces unit-by-unit inspection.

8. Inspection is recorded against a checklist at the bench in Zone F: outer packaging condition, inner seal integrity, labelling and batch or expiry where applicable, leakage, wetting, contamination, odour, temperature condition for chilled goods from Zone E, and evidence of use, opening or tampering. The inspector's name, date and time are recorded with each pallet.

9. Any goods found damaged, leaking, wet, open, out-of-temperature or suspect during returns inspection are segregated immediately. They are booked to quarantine status in the WMS, labelled as quarantine, and moved to the physically separated quarantine area in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09. They are never held in the returns inspection lanes.

10. Hazardous materials presented as returns are identified at document check and inspection. They are handled only under PR-13, stored only inside the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m² in Zone F subject to the 4,000 kg cage limit, and never leave the cage until disposition is decided.

11. On completion of inspection, returns staff propose a disposition for each inspected quantity as restock, rework or scrap. The proposal is entered in the WMS with condition, quantity proposed for each route and reason, and the goods remain in Zone F pending approval. No returned goods are restocked, reworked or scrapped without that proposal.

12. No returned goods leave Zone F without final disposition approval. Goods remain clearly identified by returns or quarantine labels and WMS status until the shift supervisor approves the disposition under PR-07. Goods overdue for inspection or awaiting approval are escalated to the shift supervisor before end of shift.

13. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone in Zone F. Speed limits of 10 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps apply to all movements to and from Zone F. Pedestrians use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers.

14. All returns receipts, 14-day eligibility checks, inspection records, quarantine transfers and proposed dispositions are logged in the WMS and retained for PR-15 handover. The shift supervisor reviews open returns, quarantine quantities and inspection exceptions on that shift and includes them in the handover record to the next supervisor.

title: Disposition and Write-Offs
text:
1. Goods in quarantine in Zone F remain physically separated and clearly identified until formally released or written off. No quarantined pallet is available for replenishment, picking or dispatch.

2. Returns staff propose disposition as restock, rework or scrap for each inspected quantity in Zone F, with reason and quantity recorded in the WMS.

3. Final disposition of inspected returns is approved only by the shift supervisor before any move from Zone F.

4. Restock is approved only where inspection shows goods are intact, sealed, correctly labelled, within expiry and, for chilled goods, with no cold-chain breach between +2 °C and +6 °C. On supervisor approval, the WMS transfers the quantity from quarantine to available stock and directs put-away from Zone F to Zone B, Zone E or to pick faces as booked stock. No hand-written location is used.

5. Rework remains in the value-added packing area in Zone F until reinspected and re-approved. Scrap is booked to scrap and held in quarantine pending disposal.

6. No inventory adjustment for restock, rework, scrap or quarantine is posted without a second count by the stock controller.

7. Harborwick applies fixed write-off approval thresholds for damaged goods. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 750 EUR. The warehouse manager approves any damaged-goods write-off above 750 EUR.

8. Thresholds are not aggregated or split to avoid escalation and approvals are not delegable. Approval is personal and recorded in the WMS and on the quarantine record with approver name, date, time, SKU, quantity, value and quarantine reference.

9. No write-off, scrap or disposal is actioned without both WMS and quarantine record entries completed.

10. Where a write-off quantity is disputed a second count is carried out and recorded before approval.

11. Open quarantine quantities, pending approvals and blocked bays are included in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

12. Any change to disposition or write-off thresholds requires prior approval by the warehouse manager.

title: Cycle Counting
text:
10. In Zone E between +2 °C and +6 °C counts are coordinated with the shift supervisor to minimise door open time. Short planned openings only are used, doors are closed between locations, and continuous monitoring and alarms remain active. No chilled pallet is removed from Zone E for counting.

All other paragraphs 1-9 and 11-13 unchanged.

title: Annual Wall-to-Wall Stocktake
text:
10. Zone E is counted with doors closed between locations and continuous monitoring and alarms between +2 °C and +6 °C remaining active, with manual verification recorded. The hazmat cage in Zone F is counted in place against the 4,000 kg limit, with no pallet removed from the cage except under PR-13 supervision.

All other paragraphs 1-9 and 11-13 unchanged, except preparation paragraphs also referencing verification stable between +2 °C and +6 °C where applicable.

title: Adjustments and Recounts
text:
9. Counts in Zone E between +2 °C and +6 °C and in the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F subject to the 4,000 kg limit are recounted in place. No chilled or hazardous pallet is removed for recounting, doors in Zone E are closed between locations, and continuous monitoring and alarms remain active.

All other paragraphs 1-8 and 10-13 unchanged.

title: Racking and Equipment Maintenance
text:
1. Racking and all handling and dock equipment are maintained under the control of the maintenance technician. The technician carries out planned checks, repairs and inspections and logs every repair and inspection in the maintenance record. No racking, truck, leveller, wrapper or barrier is returned to service after a defect affecting safety or capacity without approval.

2. High-bay pallet racking in Zone B receives a documented safety inspection every month. The inspection covers all racking in the 2,200 m² bulk area with its 2,400 pallet positions, including uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, floor fixings, beam connectors and load signs. The check also covers designated block-stack areas for compliance with the 3-pallet-high and 4.0 m-high limits.

3. The monthly inspection is carried out only by the maintenance technician on a dated PR-10 inspection sheet. Results are recorded bay by bay against the 2,700 kg bay limit, with photographs of any damage, location references and a clear pass, monitor or block decision for each bay.

4. Any damage to uprights, beams, bracing or fixings, any deflection, impact mark or missing pin, or any defect affecting the 2,700 kg rack bay limit is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The bay is blocked in the WMS and physically barriered off. No put-away, retrieval or replenishment is directed to a blocked bay.

5. A blocked bay is not returned to use until repaired, re-inspected and cleared. Repairs affecting load capacity, beam levels or rack configuration require prior approval by the warehouse manager before return to service, with the approval, date and name retained in the maintenance file.

6. The monthly inspection also includes physical separation and dock equipment. The technician checks fixed yellow barriers for the 1.2 m walkways, main transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack aisles of 3.0 m for clear width and markings, pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramp markings, and the eight dock levellers at 1.2 m height for structure, lip, controls and interlocks.

7. Materials handling equipment receives separate planned maintenance. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks, 12 hand pallet jacks, 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, 1 cardboard baler and 20 handheld scanners are maintained to manufacturer schedules, in addition to the documented daily pre-use check by the operator before first use each day.

8. Every repair and inspection is logged. The log records date, time, equipment or bay ID, zone, defect found, action taken, parts used, technician and operator names, downtime and, where required, warehouse manager approval for return to service. Daily check sheets, monthly racking sheets and repair logs are kept together for audit.

9. Any defect found during daily checks or during operations — including brakes, steering, forks, chains, mast, seat belt, lights, horn, battery or scanner bracket on trucks, or leveller, wrapper, baler or barrier faults — is reported at once to the shift supervisor, the truck or equipment is tagged out with keys removed and a do-not-use notice, and the maintenance technician is notified.

10. Defects affecting safety, capacity or stability are escalated to the warehouse manager. This includes any fault on the 1,000 kg pallet limit, 2,700 kg bay limit, 4,000 kg hazmat cage limit, load handling, braking, steering or leveller operation. No temporary fix or verbal clearance permits use.

11. The technician keeps the site plan, WMS location master and posted rack signs aligned. Any change to rack layout, bay capacity, aisle widths, barrier positions, leveller controls or fleet numbers and ratings requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and an update to the WMS locations and site plan before use.

12. Open defects, blocked bays, tagged equipment and pending approvals are included in the PR-15 handover between supervisors. The incoming supervisor checks that blocked locations remain blocked in the WMS until the logged clearance is signed.

title: Cold-Chain and Hazmat Response
text:
1. Cold-chain and hazmat response on site is controlled under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. PR-12 applies to the 300 m² cold zone Zone E held between +2 °C and +6 °C. PR-13 applies to the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m² in Zone F and to any hazardous material found in Zones A to F.

2. Zone E is fitted with continuous electronic temperature monitoring and audible alarms that activate immediately if temperature leaves the +2 °C to +6 °C range. Alarms are audible inside Zone E and at the shift supervisor's station. No alarm is silenced, reset or ignored without investigation by the shift supervisor.

6. The maintenance technician is notified at once and inspects the refrigeration plant, doors, seals, monitoring and alarm system, and logs every check and repair. Zone E is not used for new put-away until temperature is verified stable between +2 °C and +6 °C and the warehouse manager approves return to service for any defect affecting holding or alarms.

All other paragraphs 3-5 and 7-13 unchanged, with all other references to +2 °C to +8 °C updated to +2 °C to +6 °C.

title: Evacuation and Assembly
text:
1. Emergency evacuation and assembly on site is controlled under PR-14. PR-14 applies to every person on site in the hall, office annex and 3,500 m² fenced yard, including employees, visitors, contractors and drivers in the marked waiting area.

2. The alarm system provides audible evacuation signalling throughout the 6,000 m² hall, Zone E, Zone F including the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage, the office annex and the yard approaches to the eight dock doors at 1.2 m height. Alarms are tested to schedule and any fault is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician and logged.

3. On hearing the evacuation alarm, all work stops immediately in Zones A to F. Put-away in Zone B, replenishment to Zone C, picking, packing, wrapping on the 2 stretch wrappers and loading or unloading at doors 1 to 8 are left safe only if safe to do so, and dock levellers are left as found. No pallet, truck or document retrieval is permitted after the alarm.

4. Escape is only by the signed emergency routes leading to the final exits, using the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers, marked pedestrian zones and crossings where provided, and keeping the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles clear for movement. No one uses lifts, dock levellers or moves behind vehicles at doors to exit.

5. The shift supervisor is the incident lead for evacuation on that shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager. The supervisor orders immediate evacuation where danger is confirmed, directs steady movement to the exits, prevents re-entry and takes charge at the assembly point.

6. The assembly point is at the marked area by the north fence in the yard. All employees, visitors and drivers assemble there by the north fence, clear of dock approaches, yard lanes and pedestrian crossings. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain worn. Drivers are accounted for by the dispatcher from the carrier assignment list for doors 1 to 8.

7. Roll call at the assembly point by the north fence is completed before anyone re-enters the building for any reason. The shift supervisor carries out roll call against the shift roster, visitor book, driver list and floater assignments, with names checked and missing persons reported at once.

8. No person leaves the assembly point by the north fence and no person re-enters the hall until the shift supervisor has completed roll call and confirmed the result. Where any person is unaccounted for, the supervisor informs the emergency services on arrival and no search is made inside the building by staff.

9. Re-entry takes place only after roll call is complete and the building is declared safe. The all-clear is given only by the emergency services or, for a drill or false alarm, by the warehouse manager or the shift supervisor acting on manager authority after verification by the maintenance technician where equipment, racking or refrigeration is involved.

10. An evacuation drill is carried out under PR-14 every quarter. The drill is scheduled by the warehouse manager, covers both 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shift patterns over the year, and includes full evacuation to the assembly point by the north fence, roll call by register and verification that no re-entry occurs before roll call is finished.

11. Each drill is recorded with date, time, shift, zones evacuated, time to complete evacuation, roll-call result, deficiencies found and names of the shift supervisor and counters. Deficiencies in routes, signage, barriers, lighting or walkway width of 1.2 m are notified to the maintenance technician and logged.

12. Every evacuation, drill or real, is reviewed by the shift supervisor on that shift. The review is logged under PR-14, open actions and equipment defects are included in the PR-15 handover between supervisors, and any change to routes, exits, assembly point by the north fence or procedures requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before use.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 - Traffic Management: Forklifts and Pedestrians
title: 1.1 Speed Limits and Transport Routes
text: Paragraph 2 changed: Inside the building the maximum speed is 8 km/h. This limit applies everywhere inside the 6,000 m² hall, including Zones A to F, packing areas, staging lanes, main transport aisles and rack storage aisles. All other paragraphs unchanged.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 - Traffic Management: Forklifts and Pedestrians
title: 1.2 Segregated Pedestrian Walkways and Dock Discipline
text:
1. Separation of people and trucks is the governing rule in all Zones A to F, at the docks and in the yard. Pedestrians and powered equipment never share an unprotected route. Walkways for people and aisles for trucks are physically separated at all times.

2. The only permitted pedestrian routes through operational areas are the physically separated walkways protected by continuous fixed yellow barriers. Every separated walkway is 1.2 m wide measured clear between barriers or between barrier and wall, with solid white borders, green infill and overhead pedestrian signage.

3. Yellow barriers are floor-fixed, continuous and impact-rated. No pallet, cage, packing material, waste, stretch film or handling equipment is placed on, against or over a barrier, and no gap is left open for convenience. Walkways are kept clear for their full 1.2 m width at all times.

4. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m separated walkways and the marked crossings. No pedestrian walks along, crosses or stands in a main transport aisle or a rack storage aisle except at a marked pedestrian crossing, and no pedestrian walks behind a vehicle at a dock or across a dock leveller unless authorised by the shift supervisor.

5. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide measured clear between racking, barriers or walls and provide the primary through routes for the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks between Zones A to F and to and from the eight dock doors. No powered truck, hand pallet jack or loaded pallet enters a 1.2 m pedestrian walkway for any reason.

6. Rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide and are for pallet put-away and retrieval in the 2,400-position high-bay racking only. They are not used as through-routes for general transport unless the WMS task requires entry to that aisle.

7. Where pedestrian and vehicle routes meet, movement is only at marked pedestrian zones, pedestrian crossings and dock ramps. Each crossing is hatched on the floor, signed and controlled by barriers or gates. No informal crossing is created or used.

8. At every marked pedestrian zone, pedestrian crossing and dock ramp the maximum speed for all powered equipment and visiting vehicles is 5 km/h, whether pedestrians are present or not. Pedestrians have priority at crossings but do not step out until eye contact is made and the vehicle has stopped.

9. The eight dock doors are dedicated by flow. Doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are inbound only for unloading in Zone A. Doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 are outbound only for loading from Zone D. No inbound unloading is permitted at an outbound door and no outbound loading at an inbound door for any reason.

10. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling for the whole site. Every carrier is assigned a specific door and time slot before arrival, and no vehicle approaches a door, is unloaded or is loaded without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher. Changes to door or slot are made only by the dispatcher.

11. Drivers report to the gate or dispatcher on arrival and then wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the 3,500 m² fenced yard. Drivers never enter the hall, never operate materials handling equipment, dock levellers or doors, and move to the door only at the assigned time.

12. No loading or unloading begins until the vehicle is correctly positioned squarely at the assigned 1.2 m door, engine stopped, parking brake applied and dock leveller safely deployed by trained warehouse staff for that vehicle only. Dock doors remain closed when not in active use and vehicles in the waiting area do not obstruct other dock approaches, yard lanes or pedestrian routes.

13. Any temporary closure of a walkway, crossing, aisle or dock approach is controlled only by the shift supervisor, who informs the dispatcher immediately and provides an alternative barriered route before work continues. Any damage to a barrier, missing marking, obscured sign or blocked walkway is reported at once to the supervisor and repaired before the route is returned to use.
