chapter_title: Chapter 3 - Restricted Zones: Cold, Hazmat and Safe Storage
title: 3.3 Racking and Free Stacking Limits
text:
1. Every pallet on site, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. This pallet limit governs all storage capacities on site, including rack bay limits in Zone B and the hazmat cage limit in Zone F. No pallet above 1,000 kg is accepted, booked or stored.

2. High-bay pallet racking in Zone B provides 2,400 pallet positions within 2,200 m². Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg in total. The bay limit is displayed on the bay load sign and in the WMS.

3. The 2,700 kg bay limit determines how many pallets a bay can hold. At the site limit of 1,000 kg, a bay holds at most 2 full-weight pallets. A third full-weight pallet would be 3,000 kg and exceeds the bay limit. Lighter pallets may allow more units only if the total bay weight remains at or below 2,700 kg and all positions are vacant and serviceable.

4. Put-away to Zone B is permitted only to a directed vacant position within the bay limit. The WMS blocks any put-away that would exceed 2,700 kg in the bay and blocks any move to a damaged, reserved or blocked bay. No hand-written location or verbal instruction replaces the system task.

5. Where block stacking is used outside racking, stacks are limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m high including the pallets, whichever is reached first. No block stack exceeds either limit for any reason, including short-term staging.

6. Block stacking is permitted only in designated block-stack areas. No block stack is placed in a 3.0 m rack storage aisle, against rack uprights, across a 4.0 m main transport aisle, against barriers, doors, evaporators or fire exits, or on any pedestrian route.

7. Only stable, undamaged and correctly wrapped pallets are stored in racking or block stacks, with the load fully within the pallet footprint and with no overhang of beams, uprights or adjacent pallets. No leaning, collapsed or unstable pallet is stored at height.

8. Any pallet found overweight, unstable, leaning, leaking, wet or with damaged wrapping or pallets is not put away and not re-stored. It is made safe in place, segregated, reported immediately to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The bay or stack location is left empty and blocked until cleared.

9. The same weight logic applies to the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m² in Zone F. Total quantity in the cage never exceeds 4,000 kg at any time, so at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets may be in the cage at once. The WMS blocks any receipt that would exceed 4,000 kg. No hazmat is stored outside the cage.

10. Racking in Zone B receives a documented safety inspection every month by the maintenance technician on a dated sheet, bay by bay against the 2,700 kg limit. Uprights, beams, bracing, base plates, floor fixings, beam connectors and load signs are checked, with photographs of damage and a pass, monitor or block decision.

11. Any damage to uprights, beams, bracing or fixings, any deflection, impact mark or missing pin, or any defect affecting the 2,700 kg bay limit or the 4.0 m stack height is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The bay or stack area is blocked in the WMS and physically barriered off. No put-away, retrieval or replenishment is directed there.

12. A blocked bay or stack area is not returned to use until repaired, re-inspected and logged. Any repair affecting load capacity, beam levels or rack configuration requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before return to service, with date, name and approval retained in the maintenance file.

13. No storage takes place outside marked rack positions and designated block-stack areas. No attachment, modification or change to rack layout, bay capacity, stacking height or designated areas is made without prior approval by the warehouse manager and update to the posted site plan and WMS locations before use.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.1 Incident Reporting and Review
text:
1. An incident is any injury to a person, near miss between people and equipment, damage to racking, pallets or equipment, spill or leak in the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F, temperature alarm or excursion in Zone E between +2 °C and +6 °C, breach of the 8 km/h, 15 km/h and 5 km/h speed limits, or any departure from PR-09, PR-13, PR-14 and this Instruction. No incident is treated as minor.

All other paragraphs unchanged.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.2 Damaged Goods, Quarantine and Returns
text:
1. Damaged, leaking, wet, open, collapsed or suspect goods are moved to quarantine in Zone F on the same day they are found under PR-09. No damaged stock remains in its original zone overnight.

2. Quarantine is a physically separated, barriered and clearly signed area in Zone F distinct from packing, returns inspection and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. Quarantine lanes are kept clear.

3. Transfer to quarantine is booked in the WMS to quarantine status before the pallet leaves its zone, with date, zone, SKU, quantity, nature of damage and finder name recorded and a quarantine label applied.

4. Goods in quarantine remain physically separated and clearly identified until formally released or written off and are not available for picking, packing or loading.

5. Damaged hazardous materials are quarantined the same day under PR-09 and PR-13 and stored only inside the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F against the 4,000 kg limit.

6. Fixed write-off approval thresholds apply: the shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 750 EUR; the warehouse manager approves any damaged-goods write-off above 750 EUR.

7. Thresholds are not aggregated or split to avoid escalation and approvals are not delegable. Each approval is personal and recorded with approver name, date, time, SKU, quantity, value and reference, and no write-off is actioned without WMS and quarantine record entries.

8. No inventory adjustment for quarantine, scrap or restock is posted without a second count.

9. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for all quarantine and returns handling in Zone F. Speed limits of 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at marked pedestrian zones, crossings and the Zone F access apply to all movements, with pedestrians using only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways. Open quarantine quantities, proposals and approvals are included in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

chapter_title: Chapter 4 - Incidents, Damage and Emergency Response
title: 4.3 Evacuation, Alarms and Drills
text:
1. Emergency evacuation and assembly is controlled under PR-14. It applies to every person in the 6,000 m² hall, the office annex and the 3,500 m² fenced yard — employees, visitors, contractors and drivers in the marked waiting area — in Zones A to F, including Zone E and the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F.

2. The alarm system provides audible evacuation signalling throughout the hall, Zone E, Zone F, the office annex and the yard approaches to the eight dock doors at 1.2 m height. Alarms are tested to schedule and any fault, failed sounder or missing signage is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician and logged.

3. On hearing the evacuation alarm, all work stops immediately in Zones A to F. Put-away in Zone B, replenishment to Zone C, picking, packing, wrapping on the 2 stretch wrappers and loading or unloading at doors 1 to 8 are left safe only if safe to do so, with dock levellers left as found. No pallet, truck, scanner or document retrieval is permitted after the alarm.

4. Escape is only by the signed emergency routes to the final exits, using the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers and the marked pedestrian zones and crossings. The 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles are kept clear for movement. No one uses lifts, dock levellers or passes behind a vehicle at a door to exit.

5. The shift supervisor is the incident lead for evacuation on that shift, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager. One supervisor is present on every shift. The supervisor orders immediate evacuation where danger is confirmed, directs steady movement to the exits, checks that toilets, Zone E and the hazmat cage are cleared, and prevents re-entry.

6. The assembly point is the marked area by the north fence in the yard, clear of dock approaches, yard lanes and pedestrian crossings. All persons move directly there and remain together. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear remain worn. Drivers are accounted for by the dispatcher from the carrier assignment list for doors 1 to 8.

7. Roll call at the assembly point by the north fence is completed before anyone re-enters the building for any reason. The shift supervisor carries out roll call against the shift roster, visitor book, driver list and floater assignments for that shift. Names are checked individually and any missing person is reported to the emergency services at once. No search inside the building is made by staff.

8. No person leaves the assembly point by the north fence and no person re-enters the hall until the shift supervisor has completed roll call and confirmed the result. This prohibition applies to employees, managers, drivers and visitors. Where any person is unaccounted for, the supervisor informs the emergency services on arrival and follows their direction.

9. Re-entry takes place only after roll call is complete and the building is declared safe. The all-clear is given only by the emergency services or, for a drill or false alarm, by the warehouse manager or the shift supervisor acting on manager authority after verification by the maintenance technician where racking, equipment, refrigeration in Zone E or ventilation in the hazmat cage is involved.

10. An evacuation drill is carried out under PR-14 every quarter. The drill is scheduled by the warehouse manager, covers both the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shift patterns over the year, and includes full evacuation from all Zones A to F to the assembly point by the north fence, roll call by register and verification that no re-entry occurs before roll call is finished.

11. Each drill is recorded with date, time, shift, zones evacuated, time to complete evacuation, roll-call result, deficiencies found and names of the shift supervisor and counters. Deficiencies in routes, signage, lighting, barriers or walkway width of 1.2 m, blocked aisles or failed alarms are notified to the maintenance technician immediately and logged.

12. Every evacuation, drill or real, is reviewed by the shift supervisor on that shift under PR-14. Open actions, equipment defects and blocked bays are included in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00 between supervisors until cleared. Any change to escape routes, exits, the assembly point by the north fence or PR-14 requires prior approval by the warehouse manager before use.

title: 1.1 Warehouse Manager - Site Accountability and Final Sign-offs
text:
1. You are the warehouse manager and you are accountable for the whole site, including operations, safety and final sign-offs.

2. You are the only person who authorises new forklift operators and overtime.

3. You own all final sign-offs for stocktaking. You personally sign off the stocktake results and the annual wall-to-wall stocktake.

4. You sign off any damaged-goods write-off above 750 EUR. No other role signs off above 750 EUR.

5. You ensure no adjustment is ever posted without a second count and that racking receives a documented safety inspection every month and an evacuation drill is run every quarter with roll call at the assembly point by the north fence.

6. You ensure all work runs under PR-01 to PR-15 in Zones A to F, with inbound at doors 1-4 and outbound at doors 5-8, within 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 or Saturday morning overtime approved by you.

7. You own fixed site standards and no change is made without your prior approval. This includes hall or yard layout, zone boundaries and zone use for Zones A 800 m2, B 2,200 m2, C 1,200 m2, D 900 m2, E 300 m2 and F 600 m2, the location and size of the hazmat cage, aisle widths of 4.0 m and 3.0 m, pedestrian walkway provision of 1.2 m with fixed yellow barriers, dock designations for doors 1-4 inbound and 5-8 outbound, time-slot arrangements, and speed limits of 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps.

title: 1.2 Shift Supervisor - Shift Leadership and Incident Ownership
text:
1. You are the shift supervisor and you run the floor on your shift 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00, one supervisor in charge of the floor at all times.

2. You control workflow between Zones A to F, control dock readiness in Zone A and Zone D, lead incident response on your shift and conduct the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

3. You review every incident report on your shift and ensure quarantine moves to Zone F happen the same day goods are found.

4. You enforce safety standards continuously. You ensure everyone on the floor wears high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear, seat belts are worn whenever a truck is moving, and the three speed limits of 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard and 5 km/h at all marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are obeyed. You ensure pedestrians use only the physically separated 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers.

5. You approve damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 750 EUR, you approve the final disposition of inspected returns as restock, rework or scrap, and you review all quarantine records. Any write-off above 750 EUR you escalate to the warehouse manager for approval.

6. You do not authorise overtime and you do not make changes to fixed site standards without warehouse manager approval.

title: 1.3 Dispatcher - Transport Booking and Dock Scheduling
text:
1. You are the dispatcher and you own dock scheduling for the whole Harborwick site. You book all transport, assign every carrier a specific door and time slot, and release every outbound load. No vehicle approaches, unloads or loads without your confirmed assignment and, for outbound, your release.

2. You book both inbound and outbound carriers against demand and cut-off. You agree the booking reference, carrier identity, load type and quantity, and you confirm the door and slot in advance. You suspend or re-plan bookings for the annual wall-to-wall stocktake shutdown and for any closure directed by the warehouse manager.

3. You assign doors strictly by flow. Doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are inbound only for unloading in Zone A. Doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 are outbound only for loading from Zone D. You never assign inbound to doors 5 to 8 or outbound to doors 1 to 4, and you do not change a designation without prior approval by the warehouse manager.

4. Every assignment records door number at 1.2 m dock height, date, time slot and carrier, and is communicated to the gate and to the shift supervisor. You are the only person who makes or changes an assignment. No change is made on the floor without your confirmation.

5. You control the arrival flow through the 3,500 m2 fenced yard. Drivers report to the gate or to you and then wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area. You call each vehicle forward only at its assigned time when the door is free and Zone A or Zone D is ready as confirmed by the shift supervisor.

6. You work to fixed site limits. You do not book or assign any delivery that would require a pallet above 1,000 kg including load, that would exceed the 2,700 kg rack bay limit in Zone B when put away, or that would take the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F above 4,000 kg. Where a booking would breach a limit you hold it in the vehicle or in Zone A and refer to the shift supervisor for partial acceptance or refusal.

7. You release every outbound load from Zone D under PR-06. You release only when the load is fully wrapped on the 2 stretch wrappers, labelled with a WMS-generated label, closed in the WMS and physically staged by door and load in the 900 m2 Zone D lanes. No unwrapped, unlabelled or unreleased pallet is released, and no loading at doors 5 to 8 begins without your release.

8. You apply vehicle capacity rules on every release. The curtain-side trailer is rated at 24,000 kg on 33 floor positions and therefore takes at most 24 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets; payload weight governs. The delivery van is rated at 1,200 kg on 6 positions and takes at most one full-weight pallet. Any consignment above 1,200 kg or requiring more than one full-weight pallet is assigned to trailer only.

9. You plan outbound throughput within the site maximum. Each of the 4 outbound doors handles 3 trailer loads per shift within 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved only by the warehouse manager. This equals 12 trailer loads or 288 full-weight pallets per shift. You do not promise a client more than 288 full-weight pallets in one shift.

10. You coordinate continuously with the shift supervisor who runs the floor. You decide which door and when; the supervisor decides how the floor prepares, stages and executes safely in Zones A to D, keeping 4.0 m main transport aisles and 1.2 m walkways with fixed yellow barriers clear. If floor readiness conflicts with the dock plan, you decide the door plan and the supervisor decides the safe method.

11. You maintain the door board, waiting-area list and load manifest with carrier, door, slot, pallet count, total weight and release status, and you record every release with load reference, date, time and your name. You inform the supervisor immediately of delays, early or late arrivals, incomplete loads and any door or leveller fault, and you re-assign slots to keep dock approaches and yard lanes clear.

12. You enforce driver discipline. Drivers never enter the hall, never operate materials handling equipment or dock levellers and never open a dock door. Dock levellers at all eight doors are operated only by trained warehouse staff for the vehicle currently assigned. You escalate any breach, any request to change site limits or any doubt on authority to the warehouse manager before action, and you include open assignments, waiting vehicles and release status in the PR-15 handover at 14:00 and 22:00.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.1 Receiving Windows and Cut-Offs
text:
1. Harborwick provides inbound receiving at doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 only. Doors 1 to 4 are inbound only at 1.2 m dock height with dock leveller. No inbound unloading is offered at outbound doors 5 to 8.

2. Standard receiving windows are Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, aligned to the two rostered shifts. All unloading, counting, inspection and system booking in Zone A takes place within these windows.

3. No routine weekend receiving is included. Saturday morning overtime in peak season is available only when approved in advance by the warehouse manager and is limited to the morning period.

4. Every inbound delivery is by prior booking. The dispatcher assigns each carrier a specific inbound door and time slot before arrival and confirms the booking reference. Harborwick will receive only carriers with a confirmed door and slot assignment.

5. Carriers must report arrival to the gate or dispatcher and wait with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the yard. Drivers do not enter the hall and do not approach a door until called forward at the assigned time. Vehicles arriving early or outside slot will be rescheduled to the next available inbound slot.

6. Harborwick commits to the document-to-booking sequence without exception. No pallet is removed from the vehicle until document check in Zone A is complete. The check verifies carrier identity, booking reference, door and slot, purchase order or inbound reference, supplier and declared pallet quantity.

7. If documents are missing, do not match the booking, or refer to unscheduled goods, unloading will be held and the client and carrier notified via the dispatcher. No goods move beyond Zone A and no booking is made until the discrepancy is resolved.

8. After accepted document check, Harborwick will unload, count and inspect in Zone A. Count is by purchase order against checked documents; inspection covers damage, wet packaging, leakage, seal and labelling integrity and, for chilled goods, temperature condition and expiry where applicable.

9. Only inspected goods in Zone A are booked into the WMS, and only booked goods are released for physical put-away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F. Uninspected goods remain in Zone A and will not be put away or made available for order fulfilment.

10. On successful booking Harborwick creates the WMS receipt and applies a scannable pallet licence plate for each accepted pallet. The receipt records SKU, quantity, pallet identity, expiry where applicable and pallet weight against the site limit of 1,000 kg per pallet including load. Pallets without a WMS licence plate are not released.

11. Goods requiring hazardous storage are checked at inspection against the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage limit of 4,000 kg in Zone F. Harborwick will not book or store quantity that would exceed that limit. Excess will be held in Zone A or in the vehicle for client decision on partial acceptance or refusal.

12. Harborwick will confirm completion of receiving by door, with date, time, accepted quantity and exceptions noted on the paperwork and in the WMS. Shortages, overages and damaged quantities are recorded at that point and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day where applicable.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.2 Dispatch Times and Load Release
text:
1. Harborwick provides outbound dispatch at doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 only. Doors 5 to 8 are outbound only at 1.2 m dock height with dock leveller. No outbound loading is offered at inbound doors 1 to 4.

2. Standard dispatch windows are Monday to Friday 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, aligned to the two rostered shifts. All packing, wrapping, staging in Zone D and loading takes place within these windows.

3. No routine weekend dispatch is included. Saturday morning overtime in peak season is available only when approved in advance by the warehouse manager and is limited to the morning period. No Saturday afternoon, Saturday night or Sunday dispatch is offered.

4. Every outbound load is by prior booking. The dispatcher assigns each carrier a specific outbound door and time slot before arrival and confirms the door, slot and load reference. Harborwick will load only carriers with a confirmed door and slot assignment and a released load.

5. Carriers must report arrival to the gate or dispatcher and wait with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the fenced yard. Drivers do not enter the hall, do not operate materials handling equipment or dock levellers, and do not approach a door until called forward at the assigned time.

6. Harborwick commits that only verified pallets are staged for dispatch. Every item picked in Zone C is scan-verified on a handheld WMS scanner — location, SKU, batch and quantity — before it is authorised for packing. No unverified, unlabelled or unwrapped pallet is placed in Zone D.

7. Packing, labelling and wrapping are completed in Zone D before staging. Each pallet is placed stable within the pallet footprint, labelled with a WMS-generated scannable label showing customer, order and destination, and wrapped on the semi-automatic stretch wrappers with the label visible and scannable after wrapping. Hand-written labels are not used.

8. Only wrapped, labelled and system-closed pallets are eligible for staging. Staging takes place solely in Zone D of 900 m², by outbound door and by load and drop sequence as shown on the WMS outbound manifest. No staging takes place outside Zone D.

9. Every outbound pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. Harborwick will not wrap, stage or load any pallet above 1,000 kg. Overweight, unstable, leaking or damaged pallets are segregated in Zone D, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day and excluded from the load.

10. No loading begins without dispatcher release. Release is given only when the complete load is wrapped, labelled, closed in the WMS and physically staged in its correct lane in Zone D, and the assigned vehicle is confirmed for that door and slot.

11. Loading at doors 5 to 8 begins only when the vehicle is correctly positioned, engine stopped, parking brake applied and dock leveller safely deployed by trained warehouse staff. Each pallet is scanned by licence plate against the released load. Any quantity, label or destination mismatch stops loading for client and dispatcher resolution.

12. Harborwick plans outbound throughput on fixed vehicle and door capacities. The contracted curtain-side trailer is rated at 24,000 kg on 33 floor positions and therefore takes at most 24 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets; the delivery van is rated at 1,200 kg on 6 positions and takes at most one full-weight pallet. Consignments above 1,200 kg are assigned to trailer only.

13. Each of the 4 outbound doors handles 3 trailer loads per shift. At 24 full-weight pallets per trailer this equates to a site maximum of 12 trailer loads or 288 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets per shift. Harborwick will not promise a client more than 288 full-weight pallets in a single shift.

14. On completion of loading Harborwick closes the load in the WMS, seals the vehicle and completes dispatch paperwork with door, carrier, load reference, pallet count, total weight, date, time and loader and dispatcher names. No vehicle is released from the yard without completed paperwork and dispatcher confirmation.

chapter_title: Chapter 1 — Inbound and Outbound Service Levels
title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
text:
1. Harborwick operates eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height, each with its own dock leveller, on the yard side of the 6,000 m² hall within the 3,500 m² fenced yard. Doors 1, 2, 3 and 4 are inbound only for unloading. Doors 5, 6, 7 and 8 are outbound only for loading. No door is used for the opposite flow for any client or carrier.

2. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling for the whole site. The dispatcher books transport, assigns every carrier a specific door and time slot, sequences loads by cut-off and carrier booking, and releases every outbound load from Zone D. No other role makes or changes a door or slot assignment.

3. Every inbound and outbound movement is by prior booking with a confirmed assignment before arrival. The assignment records door number, date, time slot, carrier and booking or load reference and is communicated to the gate and the shift supervisor. Harborwick will not receive or load a vehicle without a confirmed assignment for that door and slot.

4. No vehicle approaches a door without instruction. On arrival carriers report to the gate or dispatcher and wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the yard. Drivers do not enter the hall, do not operate materials handling equipment, dock levellers or doors, and move to the door only at the assigned time when called forward.

5. A vehicle that arrives early, late or without a booking waits only in the marked waiting area and is rescheduled to the next available slot for that flow by the dispatcher. Vehicles do not obstruct other dock approaches, yard lanes or pedestrian routes while waiting. The dispatcher informs the shift supervisor of any delay, rescheduling or door closure immediately.

6. Door changes, time-slot changes and re-bookings are made only by the dispatcher. Floor staff do not reassign doors. Where Zone A or Zone D is not ready, the shift supervisor advises the dispatcher, who decides the revised door plan while the supervisor decides the safe method of work on the floor.

7. Harborwick applies a fixed site pallet limit to all transport planning. Every pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. Harborwick will not accept, book, stage or load any pallet above 1,000 kg. Any pallet presented above that limit is held for client decision and excluded from throughput calculations.

8. Vehicle capacities offered to clients are fixed and governed by weight before floor space. The contracted curtain-side trailer is rated at 24,000 kg payload on 33 floor positions and therefore takes at most 24 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets. Where pallets weigh less than 1,000 kg, additional pallets may be loaded to use floor space provided the 24,000 kg payload is not exceeded and the load is stable.

9. The delivery van is rated at 1,200 kg payload on 6 floor positions and takes at most one full-weight 1,000 kg pallet. No van is loaded beyond 1,200 kg. Any consignment exceeding 1,200 kg or requiring more than one full-weight pallet is assigned to trailer and loaded only at doors 5 to 8.

10. Hazardous consignments are planned within the same scheduling system and against the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage limit of 4,000 kg in Zone F, meaning at most 4 full-weight pallets in the cage at any time. Harborwick will not schedule or accept inbound hazmat that would exceed that limit.

11. Promised outbound throughput is fixed by doors and turn rate. Each of the 4 outbound doors handles 3 trailer loads per shift within 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, or during Saturday morning overtime approved in advance by the warehouse manager. This equates to 12 trailer loads per shift.

12. At 24 full-weight pallets per trailer, the site maximum is 288 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets per shift. This is the most Harborwick will promise a single client or a group of clients for one shift. Client orders exceeding that volume will be scheduled across consecutive shifts or days by the dispatcher in agreement with the client.

13. Any change to door designations, time-slot arrangements, vehicle ratings or the 288-pallet shift maximum requires prior approval by the warehouse manager and advance notice to clients before it is offered as a service level.

title: 2.1 Order Accuracy and Picking Service Level
text:
1. Harborwick provides order picking only from Zone C of 1,200 m², comprising ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Zone C holds no bulk reserve, no quarantine stock and no hazardous materials. All pick faces in Zone C are fed exclusively by replenishment from bulk storage in Zone B.

2. Replenishment of pick faces is carried out under PR-03 before each picking shift within 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00. Harborwick commits that no picking wave starts until the shift supervisor has confirmed replenishment complete and Zone C released for picking.

3. Replenishment is system-directed via the WMS. Tasks are generated from current pick-face levels, open customer orders and available booked stock in Zone B, and are executed by authorised forklift operators on handheld scanners against the 2,400 bulk positions and the rack bay limit of 2,700 kg.

4. Picking is carried out under PR-04 on scanner-directed tasks only. Ten pickers work in Zone C on the 20 handheld WMS scanners, following the WMS wave, sequence and face. Flow racks are picked from the front pick side only. No paper picks, verbal instructions or memory picks are used.

5. Harborwick commits to 100% scan verification of every picked item before packing. At each face the picker scans the pick-face location label and then scans each SKU, batch, expiry where applicable, and quantity as directed. The WMS verifies all three before authorising packing.

6. A pick is accepted only where location matches task, SKU and batch match order, and quantity matches directed quantity. The WMS closes the pick line only on that three-way match. No forced confirmation or manual override is permitted on the scanner.

7. Any scan failure stops the pick at that face. Wrong SKU, wrong batch, wrong expiry, wrong quantity or unreadable barcode is recorded as scan-failed on the scanner, stock is left in place and the shift supervisor is notified immediately for face check, recount by the stock controller or re-directed replenishment.

8. Damaged, leaking, wet, open or suspect goods found at the face are not picked and not verified. They are segregated, reported to the shift supervisor and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09, with the exception recorded in the WMS.

9. Where the face quantity is insufficient, the picker records the actual quantity picked and confirms short pick on the scanner. Harborwick logs the shortage as a verified short pick, retains the order line as incomplete and triggers replenishment from Zone B. No substitution from another face is made without a new WMS task.

10. Only scan-verified lines are authorised for packing and labelling. Packing under PR-05 begins only after WMS authorisation for that order or pallet. Goods are placed stable within the pallet footprint under the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg including load.

11. Labelling accuracy is WMS-controlled. Labels are applied only to scan-verified and packed pallets in Zone D, after scanning the pallet licence plate and applying the WMS-generated label showing customer, order and destination. Hand-written or non-matching labels are not used.

12. On completion of a wave, Harborwick closes the verified pallet in the WMS as ready for Zone D, recording picker name, scanner ID, date and time and linking the pallet to its order and outbound load. Only closed, scan-verified pallets are transferred to dispatch staging in Zone D.

13. All scan verifications, failures, short picks, quarantine moves and packing completions are recorded automatically in the WMS. Harborwick makes the verification record available to the client on request and reviews exceptions during the shift for correction before dispatch.

14. Any scanner fault, label misprint or system rejection that prevents verification holds the affected pallet in Zone C. Harborwick will not move the pallet to Zone D, wrap or load it until the fault is corrected and successful scan verification is completed on a serviceable scanner.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.1 Damaged Goods and Quarantine Handling
text:
1. Harborwick handles all damaged, leaking, wet, open, collapsed or suspect goods under PR-09. Any such goods found in Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone or Zone F itself are moved to quarantine in Zone F on the same day they are found. No damaged stock remains in its original zone overnight.

2. Quarantine is located in Zone F within the 600 m² services and control area. It is a physically separated, barriered and clearly signed area, distinct from packing, returns inspection and the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage. Harborwick keeps quarantine lanes clear and available at all times.

3. Harborwick commits to the same-day quarantine standard for every client. On finding damage the floor staff secure the area, report immediately to the shift supervisor and transfer the pallet to Zone F only on supervisor direction. No sorting, re-stacking or disposal takes place at the original location.

4. Transfer to quarantine is booked in the WMS to quarantine status before the pallet leaves its zone. Harborwick records date, zone and location found, SKU, batch and expiry where applicable, quantity, pallet identity, nature of damage and finder name, and applies a quarantine label. Goods booked to quarantine status are not available for replenishment, picking or dispatch.

5. Goods in quarantine remain physically separated and clearly identified by quarantine label and WMS status until formally released or written off. Harborwick will not pick, pack or load any quarantined pallet for any client order.

6. Damaged goods from receiving inspection in Zone A are not counted as available stock. Harborwick segregates them in Zone A, books them to quarantine status only and moves them to Zone F the same day, recording the quantity, damage type and pallet reference for write-off approval.

7. Damaged bulk or pick-face stock found during storage in Zone B, replenishment to Zone C or dispatch staging in Zone D is removed from its location immediately. Harborwick leaves the affected bay, face or lane empty and blocks it in the WMS where applicable until cleared.

8. Damaged hazardous materials are quarantined the same day under PR-09 and PR-13 and stored only inside the separate 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F. Harborwick counts the quantity against the cage limit of 4,000 kg at all times, meaning at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets, and never holds damaged hazmat outside the cage.

9. Damaged chilled goods from Zone E are segregated in place, booked to quarantine status where required and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day. Harborwick does not return them to Zone E and does not pick, pack or load them pending disposition.

10. Harborwick applies fixed write-off approval thresholds for every client. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 750 EUR. The warehouse manager approves any damaged-goods write-off above 750 EUR. Thresholds are not aggregated or split to avoid escalation and approvals are not delegable.

11. Approval is personal and recorded in the WMS and on the quarantine record with approver name, date, time, SKU, quantity, value and quarantine reference. Harborwick will not action a write-off, scrap or disposal without both entries completed.

12. No inventory adjustment for quarantine, scrap or restock is posted without a second count under PR-08. Where a write-off quantity is disputed, Harborwick will carry out the second count via the stock controller and record the result before approval is given.

13. Harborwick notifies the client of each quarantine event on the daily exceptions report, with date, location, SKU, quantity, reason and WMS quarantine reference, and provides photographs where racking, pallet or product damage is involved. Open quarantine quantities, pending approvals and blocked bays, including any bay affected by the 2,700 kg limit in Zone B, are included in the weekly inventory report until cleared.

14. Scrapped quantities remain in quarantine, clearly marked as scrap and segregated by product type, pending collection for disposal. Harborwick does not return scrapped food, drugstore or hazmat quantities to Zone C or Zone D and retains the full audit trail of quarantine moves, second counts and threshold approvals for client review.

chapter_title: Chapter 3 — Damaged Goods, Returns and Temperature-Controlled Storage
title: 3.2 Returns Handling and Disposition
text:
1. Harborwick handles all returns under PR-07 in Zone F within the 600 m² services and control area. All returned goods are received, recorded and inspected only in the returns inspection area in Zone F. No returns are inspected, stored or dispositioned in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D or Zone E, and no returns are handled at outbound doors 5 to 8.

2. Harborwick accepts returns within 14 calendar days of the original delivery date only. The delivery date is taken from the outbound manifest and proof of delivery for that load, counted as calendar days from delivery to presentation at site. Returns presented after 14 days are not accepted.

3. All returns arrive by prior booking at an assigned inbound door 1 to 4 at a time slot agreed with the dispatcher. The dispatcher assigns door and slot before arrival. Carriers report to the gate or dispatcher and wait only with their vehicle or in the marked driver waiting area in the fenced yard.

4. Before unloading Harborwick checks returns paperwork in Zone A: customer name, original order and outbound load reference, delivery date, SKU and quantity presented, and reason for return. The 14-day eligibility and door and slot assignment are verified at that point.

5. Where the delivery was more than 14 days ago, the customer or order cannot be matched, or the quantity would breach the site pallet limit of 1,000 kg including load or the 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage limit of 4,000 kg in Zone F, Harborwick will refuse the return at the door. Refusal is recorded with date, time, door, carrier and reason and countersigned by the shift supervisor.

6. Accepted returns are moved directly to Zone F and booked in the WMS to returns status on arrival, with customer, original order, delivery date, return date, SKU, quantity, pallet identity and reason. They are physically separated, clearly signed as returns and are not available for picking, replenishment or dispatch.

7. Harborwick commits to unit-by-unit inspection of every returned item in Zone F. Inspection is carried out by the returns and packing staff under PR-07 against a bench checklist: outer packaging, inner seal integrity, labelling and batch or expiry, leakage, wetting, contamination, odour, temperature condition for chilled goods, and evidence of use or tampering.

8. Inspection is recorded with inspector name, date and time per pallet or unit in the WMS. No bulk acceptance or sample check replaces individual inspection. Goods remain in returns status in Zone F until inspection and proposal are complete.

9. Any goods found damaged, leaking, wet, open, out-of-temperature or suspect during returns inspection are segregated immediately. Harborwick books them to quarantine status in the WMS, labels them as quarantine and moves them to the physically separated quarantine area in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09.

10. Hazardous materials presented as returns are handled only under PR-13. They are stored only inside the separate 60 m² ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F, subject at all times to the 4,000 kg cage limit, meaning at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets, with incompatible classes segregated as marked.

11. On completion of inspection Harborwick proposes disposition for each inspected quantity in the WMS as restock, rework or scrap, with condition, quantity for each route and reason. No returned goods are restocked, reworked or scrapped without that proposal entered.

12. Final disposition of all inspected returns is approved only by the shift supervisor before any move from Zone F. Restock is approved only where goods are intact, sealed, correctly labelled and within expiry and cold-chain; rework remains in the value-added packing area in Zone F until reinspected and re-approved; scrap is booked to scrap and held in quarantine pending disposal.

13. No inventory adjustment for restock, rework or scrap is posted without a second count under PR-08. Where a quantity is disputed, Harborwick will carry out the second count via the stock controller and record the result before approval. Write-off thresholds for damaged quantities apply as per PR-09.

14. Harborwick retains the full audit trail for each return: eligibility check, receipt to returns status, inspection record, quarantine transfer where applicable, proposed disposition and supervisor approval with name, date and WMS reference. The client is notified of acceptance, refusal, inspection outcome and final disposition on the daily exceptions report.

title: 3.3 Temperature-Controlled Storage SLA
text:
1. Harborwick provides temperature-controlled storage only in Zone E within the 6,000 m² hall. Zone E is a physically segregated, insulated enclosure of 300 m² with self-closing doors, held continuously between +2 °C and +6 °C under PR-12. No chilled storage is offered in any other zone.

2. Harborwick commits to maintain Zone E between +2 °C and +6 °C at all times while goods are stored. The commitment applies to standard operating hours 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 Monday to Friday and to any Saturday morning overtime approved by the warehouse manager.

3. Zone E is fitted with continuous electronic temperature monitoring and audible alarms that activate immediately if temperature leaves the +2 °C to +6 °C range. Alarms are audible inside Zone E and at the shift supervisor's station. No alarm is silenced, reset or ignored without investigation by the shift supervisor.

9. Harborwick commits to immediate cold-chain response. Any alarm, excursion outside +2 °C to +6 °C, door fault, icing, condensation, leakage or evidence of breach is reported immediately to the shift supervisor, who secures stock in place, closes doors and prevents any picking in Zone C, packing or dispatch of affected pallets.

11. No new put-away to Zone E takes place during an active alarm or verified excursion. Harborwick will not accept new chilled receipts into Zone E until temperature is verified stable between +2 °C and +6 °C and any defect to refrigeration, doors, monitoring or alarms is inspected and logged by the maintenance technician.

All other paragraphs 4-8 and 12-14 unchanged, with all occurrences of +8 °C updated to +6 °C.
